Elastic limit

Words: 29
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
The boundary of the loading range within which a material recovers its original configuration on unloading. Elasticity need not be linear; beyond the elastic range, permanent plastic deformation or damage may remain.

Brittle fracture

Words: 109 Articles: 2
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
Failure by crack formation or propagation with limited distributed permanent deformation. Shear and opening fractures have different strength conditions; a frictional failure envelope should not be extrapolated indefinitely into tension.

Shear failure

Words: 38
Brittle fracture OurBigBook.com
Loss of load-bearing strength accompanied by relative displacement tangential to a surface, rather than primarily opening normal to it. The Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion models frictional shear failure by ∣τ∣=c+μσn′​, using cohesion, a friction coefficient and compressive effective stress normal to the potential sliding plane.

Tensile failure criterion (σ3′​=−T0​)

Words: 43
Brittle fracture OurBigBook.com
In the simplest strength-cutoff model, opening begins when the least compressive effective stress reaches minus the tensile strength: σ3′​=−T0​ with compression positive. In Mohr's circle, this is contact with the vertical line σn′​=−T0​ at τ=0. The criterion represents an opening mechanism and differs from frictional shear failure.

Elastic modulus

Words: 19
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
A coefficient relating an appropriate stress and strain in the linear elastic regime. Young's modulus, shear modulus and bulk modulus describe different deformation modes.

Buckling

Words: 75 Articles: 1
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
Loss of stability of a loaded configuration toward a bent or folded form. The threshold and deformation mode depend on geometry, material properties and boundary conditions.

Buckling of a synthetic film (κq4+σq2<0)

Words: 49
Buckling OurBigBook.com
A flat, unsupported film's bending and tension energies give modal stiffness κq4+σq2. Negative tension represents compression, destabilizing sufficiently long waves. A finite sheet restricts allowed wave numbers, while a supporting foundation adds stiffness and can select a wrinkle wavelength. This is generic continuum mechanics, independent of biological membrane structure.

Eigenstrain (ε∗)

Words: 26
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
An eigenstrain is a local preferred deformation in the absence of stress. Constraints or incompatibility can make the actual strain differ from it, generating stress. Magnetostrictive strain is one example.

Magnetoelastic coupling

Words: 21
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
Magnetoelastic coupling links a material's magnetic state to its strain and stress. Magnetostriction describes a resulting deformation; mechanical loading can also change the magnetic state.

Elastic deformation

Words: 48
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
An elastic deformation is recoverable when the deforming loads are removed. In a local elastic constitutive model the stress depends on the present deformation. When this response also derives from a stored elastic energy, the material is a hyperelastic material. In the small-deformation approximation, the relevant kinematic variable is the infinitesimal strain tensor.

Perfectly bonded elastic interface ([u]=0,[σ]n=0)

Words: 113 Articles: 1
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
A perfectly bonded elastic interface has continuous displacement field and continuous traction, with the same chosen normal on both sides. For piecewise affine displacement fields, the difference of their gradients annihilates every tangential vector, and hence has the form a⊗n. Their infinitesimal strain tensors differ by sym(a⊗n).

Torsion and tilt stiffness of a bonded elastic disk (KV​=πGa4/(2h),KH​=πMa4/(4h))

Words: 72
Perfectly bonded elastic interface OurBigBook.com
A circular elastic layer of thickness h≪a bonded between rigid faces develops shear strain rϕ/h under a relative twist ϕ. Integrating the shear stress times its moment arm gives KV​=GJp​/h. A small relative tilt produces longitudinal strain yθ/h; when lateral deformation is constrained, the corresponding normal traction gives KH​=MI/h. The polar second moment of area is Jp​=πa4/2 and the diametric second moment of area is I=πa4/4. Edge relaxation limits this thin-layer approximation, especially in a nearly incompressible material.

Static elastic equilibrium (σij,j​+fi​=0)

Words: 33
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
A symmetric stress tensor is in static elastic equilibrium when its divergence balances the prescribed body force. Its boundary traction is ti​=σij​nj​. With zero body force, integration by parts gives ∫Ω​σ:sym∇v=∫∂Ω​t⋅v. This is the weak principle of virtual work for a static elastic body.

Elastic beam

Words: 601 Articles: 8
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
An elastic beam is a slender body that supports bending moments and transverse loads. In the small-slope Euler-Bernoulli approximation its bending moment is M=EIyxx​, and transverse momentum balance gives ρAytt​+EIyxxxx​=q for a uniform beam under distributed force per length q. Here I is the second moment of area; boundary conditions specify the end constraints and applied moments and forces.

Transverse shear force (N)

Words: 36
Elastic beam OurBigBook.com
The component of the internal resultant force perpendicular to an elastic beam's tangent. For a planar elastic beam, one consistent sign convention has bending moment M=−Bw′′ and M′=N, so N=−Bw′′′. Reversing the section or bending moment convention reverses the corresponding signs.

Euler strut

Words: 180 Articles: 1
Elastic beam OurBigBook.com
An Euler strut is an initially straight slender elastic column loaded in axial compression. Its lateral stability depends on bending stiffness, length and endpoint constraints. Euler buckling predicts a loss of straight-configuration stability before material failure only in the appropriate slender elastic regime; it is distinct from crushing or plastic yielding of a short column.

Critical-load minimality of the angular Euler strut (λ=1:U[θ]>U[0] for θ=0,δ2U[0] is degenerate)

Words: 131
Euler strut OurBigBook.com
For the angular endpoint conditions θ(0)=θ(1)=0, take U=(EI/L)∫01​[θ′2/2−π2λ(1−cosθ)]dξ. The Poincaré inequality and 1−cost≤t2/2 give U≥0 for 0≤λ≤1. At λ=1 a nonzero continuous angle still has strictly positive energy because 1−cost<t2/2 for t=0. Thus the straight state remains the unique global minimum at the critical parameter even though the quadratic variation vanishes on the first sine mode.
Along that mode the energy is π2EIA4/(64L)+O(A6) at criticality. For λ>1 a sufficiently small first-mode variation lowers energy, so the straight state loses local minimality. Near the first threshold, expansion of the Euler strut equation gives A0​(A02​−8λ1​)=0 when λ=1+ϵλ1​ and θ∼ϵ​A0​sinπξ. The resulting supercritical pitchfork bifurcation is stabilized by the same positive quartic term. A zero second variation is therefore an inconclusive quadratic test, not proof of failure of minimization.

Euler elastica (EIθ′′+Fsinθ=0)

Words: 230 Articles: 2
Elastic beam OurBigBook.com
The planar equilibrium of an inextensible slender beam can have large tangent angle while retaining small elastic strain across its thickness. For constant horizontal compressive force F, moment balance and curvature θ′=dθ/ds give the displayed nonlinear equation. Multiplication by θ′ gives the first integral EIθ′2/2−Fcosθ=C. A tensile load has F<0 in this convention.

Endpoint position compatibility for the Euler elastica (Δy=∫0L​sinθds)

Words: 121
Euler elastica OurBigBook.com
Specifying endpoint tangent angles of an inextensible rod does not by itself specify its endpoint positions. A planar Euler elastica satisfies x′=cosθ, y′=sinθ, so equal endpoint heights require the displayed integral to vanish. For constant compressive resultant (−P,0), the angular equation is EIθ′′+Psinθ=0, giving PΔy=−EI[θ′(L)−θ′(0)]. Thus a nontrivial branch containing an odd number of pendulum half-periods cannot have equal endpoint heights and the same zero endpoint angles with zero transverse resultant. At small amplitude the tangent-only eigenfunctions are sin(nπs/L), with Pn​=EI(nπ/L)2; equal endpoint heights retain even n and give the first fixed-clamp load 4π2EI/L2. Other clamp modes can require a nonzero transverse reaction. Axial shortening is also needed when the reference endpoint separation equals the rod length.

Tensile elastica loop (θ=4arctanesT/(EI)​)

Words: 58
Euler elastica OurBigBook.com
An ideal zero-thickness planar loop under tension T is a separatrix of the elastica equation. Its tangent turns from zero to 2π, the same physical orientation at both ends. With α=T/(EI)​, integration gives x=s−2tanh(αs)/α and y=2sech(αs)/α. Its height is 2EI/T​. Self-contact and finite beam thickness are absent from this ideal crossing solution.

Cantilever

Words: 98 Articles: 1
Elastic beam OurBigBook.com
A beam fixed at one end and free at the other. A transverse end force F gives bending moment M(x)=F(L−x) and, for a rectangular section, maximum bending stress 6FL/(wh2) at the fixed end. Longitudinal tension and compression are greatest on opposite outer fibres.

Self-weight deflection of a square cantilever (y(l)=3ρgl4/(2Ea2))

Words: 55
Cantilever OurBigBook.com
A uniform square section has second moment of area a4/12 and gravitational load per length ρga2. Euler-Bernoulli bending therefore gives y′′′′=12ρg/(Ea2), with zero displacement and slope at the clamp and zero moment and shear at the free end. Integrating gives the displayed tip deflection and y(x)=ρgx2(x2−4lx+6l2)/(2Ea2). Small slope and strain are required.

Dead loading

Words: 202 Articles: 2
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
In an elastic boundary value problem, a dead load is a prescribed force independent of the incremental displacement. A dead reference traction has δt0=0, even when the current face changes orientation. This differs from a follower load, whose direction follows the moving body, and from the structural-engineering use of the same phrase for permanent self-weight. Under pure dead tractions, a constant incremental translation remains a zero-frequency mode unless a displacement condition fixes it.

Stretch-sum degeneracy of an equally dead-loaded incompressible cube (v1​+v2​+v3​=τ/μ,v1​v2​v3​=1)

Words: 93
Dead loading OurBigBook.com
For Φ=μ[∑i​vi2​/2+∑i​vi−1​] and positive stretch product one, the energy simplifies to μS2/2, where S=∑i​vi​. Equal nominal tensile loading adds potential −τS. The homogeneous diagonal equilibrium equations reduce to (μS−τ)(vi​−vj​)=0. Thus the unit triple exists for every load, while the other equilibria form the displayed sum-product family. Since S≥3, only the unit triple exists for τ≤3μ. Above this load, a continuous family is obtained by choosing v1​=t near one and taking v2​,v3​ as the two positive roots with sum τ/μ−t and product 1/t.

Dead-load traction (tR​(X))

Words: 37
Dead loading OurBigBook.com
A dead-load traction is prescribed force per unit reference surface area, with its vector held fixed as the body deforms. Its boundary condition is TR​N=tR​. A follower load instead depends on the current deformation, for example through a current normal or current area.

Magnetostriction

Words: 1k Articles: 11
Elasticity (physics) OurBigBook.com
Magnetostriction is a change of a material's shape or dimensions associated with its magnetization. A magnetic field can therefore produce strain without a contact force. The resulting magnetoelastic coupling lets a ferromagnet convert changes of magnetic state into mechanical motion; a constraint can instead turn the preferred deformation into stress. James Prescott Joule published his study of iron and steel bars in 1847.[ref]
The surprising point is that reversing the magnetization need not reverse the deformation. A material can prefer a longer axis along either +m or −m: an axis has no arrow. Isotropic linear magnetostriction vanishes excludes one particular linear constitutive term, while saturated isotropic magnetostrictive strain supplies a nonzero response with a quadratic dependence on the magnetic direction. The pulsed-field optical magnetostriction experiment shows how an actual length change can be resolved, and quadratic magnetostriction and frequency doubling separates an illustrative response law from a measured material curve.

Strain-mediated magnetoelectric coupling

Words: 40
Magnetostriction OurBigBook.com
Coupling in which a magnetic material's preferred strain transfers mechanical stress to a piezoelectric constituent, producing an electrical response. It depends on interfaces, elastic load sharing and electrical boundary conditions; a composite's measured voltage is not by itself an intrinsic single-phase magnetoelectric coefficient.

Magnetostrictive actuator

Words: 21
Magnetostriction OurBigBook.com
A magnetostrictive actuator uses magnetostriction to produce displacement or force. Its free motion and its blocked stress are different boundary conditions, as shown in free strain and blocked magnetostrictive stress.

Magnetostrictive strain (εijmag​)

Words: 74 Articles: 2
Magnetostriction OurBigBook.com
Magnetostrictive strain is the preferred strain associated with a specified magnetic state relative to a stated reference. The measured strain also depends on mechanical constraints.

Volume magnetostriction (ΔV/V)

Words: 28
Magnetostrictive strain OurBigBook.com
Volume magnetostriction is the relative volume change associated with a magnetic-state change. To first order it is the trace of the magnetostrictive strain. Zero trace is an additional restriction, not a consequence of isotropy alone.

Saturation magnetostriction (λs​)

Consider a mechanically free isotropic model of a saturated ferromagnet, at fixed temperature and fixed magnitude of magnetization. Let m=M/Ms​ be a unit vector, where Ms​ is the saturation magnetization. The magnetostrictive strain is an infinitesimal strain tensor, measured relative to a reference with randomly oriented magnetic domains. This reference convention matters: it sets the orientational average of the preferred strain to zero. Define λs​, the saturation magnetostriction, as the longitudinal relative length change in this model.
Rotational symmetry permits a symmetric second-rank tensor made from m of the form aδij​+bmi​mj​, where δij​ is the Kronecker delta. If we restrict attention to a change of shape with zero first-order volume change, its trace gives 3a+b=0. Requiring the longitudinal component to equal λs​ gives a+b=λs​. Hence
εijmag​=23λs​​(mi​mj​−3δij​​),ε∥​=λs​,ε⊥​=−2λs​​.
(1)
The tensor product m⊗m is symmetric and unchanged under m↦−m. It uses two copies of the magnetic direction, so the third-rank isotropic tensor obstruction in isotropic linear magnetostriction vanishes does not apply. More generally, a small-magnetization expansion can contain aM2δij​+bMi​Mj​; isotropy alone does not require its trace to vanish. The displayed saturated formula isolates the volume-preserving orientational contribution, rather than asserting that every material has zero volume magnetostriction.
Along a measuring unit vector n, with n⋅m=cosθ, the fractional length change is
LΔLn​​=ni​εijmag​nj​=2λs​​(3cos2θ−1).
(2)
For a stipulated λs​=20×10−6 and reference length L=100mm, alignment gives +2μm and a perpendicular orientation gives −1μm. Rotating from perpendicular to parallel therefore changes the length by 3μm, even though the saturated longitudinal value relative to the random reference is 2μm. A negative λs​ reverses these elongation and contraction signs.
The eigenvalues of this infinitesimal strain tensor are λs​,−λs​/2,−λs​/2, so ΔV/V=trεmag=0 to first order. This is not exact finite incompressibility: using the illustrative deformation gradient F=I+εmag gives
detF=(1+λs​)(1−λs​/2)2=1−43​λs2​+41​λs3​.
(3)
A finite-deformation law would need higher-order corrections if exact volume conservation were required.

Saturated isotropic magnetostrictive strain OurBigBook.com
A full 180∘ reversal leaves saturated isotropic magnetostrictive strain unchanged. A 90∘ rotation generally changes it. In the simplest unconstrained orientation average over magnetic domains, replace mi​mj​ by ⟨mi​mj​⟩, not by ⟨mi​⟩⟨mj​⟩. Equal populations pointing along +z and −z have zero net magnetization but the same preferred strain as a single domain along z. An isotropic orientation distribution instead has ⟨mi​mj​⟩=δij​/3 and zero average preferred strain. Elastic compatibility between real magnetic domains can modify the macroscopic response.
Reversing an applied magnetic field does not guarantee that all microscopic orientations retrace the same path. Hysteresis, magnetic domain-wall pinning, and changes in domain populations can alter the measured curve. The reversal identity concerns the same pair of magnetic states with opposite local magnetization; it is not a universal prediction that an arbitrary experimental sweep is a single-valued even function of applied magnetic field.

Pulsed-field optical magnetostriction experiment

Words: 247
Magnetostriction OurBigBook.com
A 3×1.5×1.5mm3 single crystal of gadolinium antimonide carried a 2mm fibre Bragg grating cyanoacrylate-bonded along its a axis. The pulsed magnetic field paralleled that axis. Broadband light, a circulator and a spectrometer resolved reflected-wavelength shifts at 5.4K. Pre-pulse readings measured noise; low fibre thermal expansion reduced thermal background. A residual post-pulse shift indicated possible heating. Spectral distortion checked bond uniformity, while the fibre's smaller cross-section limited loading; bonding was not assumed force-free. Longitudinal strain showed a kink near 32.6T.[ref]
The distinction between readout and inference is essential. The fibre Bragg grating senses a change of reflected wavelength; interpreting this as the specimen's strain requires good strain transfer and a controlled temperature. A useful independent control would compare a bonded sensor with a nearby unloaded sensor through the same pulse. Another would vary bond stiffness or specimen cross-section to test loading. These are proposed checks, not additional procedures claimed for the experiment above. The pulsed magnet's winding details were not specified in the inspected account.
This experiment measures one longitudinal component of strain. Establishing the first-order volume change would require three orthogonal normal components under the same conditions. GdSb also has its own antiferromagnetism and field-dependent magnetic structure: this measured curve does not establish the simple saturated isotropic law. Its role here is to make the measurement chain and its limitations concrete.

Young's modulus is the ratio of axial stress to axial strain in uniaxial linear elasticity. For an isotropic plate, the bending rigidity is Et3/[12(1−ν2)], with thickness t and Poisson's ratio ν.
A tensile modulus experiment asks how much a specimen stretches under an axial force, while allowing its sides to contract freely. For initial cross-sectional area A0​ and an extensometer spanning initial gauge length Lg​, define engineering stress σ=F/A0​ and engineering strain ε=ΔLg​/Lg​. In the proportional range,
E=dεdσ​=A0​Lg​​d(ΔLg​)dF​.
(13)
The ratio σ/ε agrees with this derivative when the line passes through the unloaded origin. A fitted offset should not be mistaken for a material property. Young's modulus has units of pressure: 1 Pa=1 Nm−2. By contrast, the spring constant of a uniform tensile specimen of length L is ks​=EA0​/L, with units Nm−1. Two rods made of the same material can therefore have very different spring constants while sharing Young's modulus.
The normalization removes a useful geometrical ambiguity: doubling L doubles the extension at a given force, whereas doubling A0​ halves it. For a round specimen A0​=πd2/4; for a rectangular one A0​=wt, using initial diameter d, width w and thickness t. Diameter error matters twice at first order: δA0​/A0​≃2δd/d. Specify material direction, temperature and loading rate when comparing Young's modulus. Lateral restraint changes the stress state and can prevent this experiment from measuring the uniaxial modulus.
The name commemorates Thomas Young, whose formulation of a measure of elasticity is recorded by the Royal Society. This attribution alone does not establish priority for every modern definition or experimental method.[ref]

MIT's Spring 2004 laboratory assignment Properties of Heat Treated Steel gives a concrete tensile testing protocol. Record transducer channels and calibration factors; measure specimen diameter and length, and the extensometer gauge length with its locking pin inserted. Zero the load cell, pin the threaded grips into their adapters, and attach the extensometer centrally. Apply the specified seating load, record actuator position, then acquire readings every second while moving at about 0.05 cmmin−1. The handout derives engineering stress from load cell force, engineering strain from extensometer deformation, and Young's modulus by linear regression below the proportional limit; it warns that actuator-derived strain includes apparatus deformation.[ref]
For a modulus-focused measurement, select a load window after seating, hold temperature and loading rate consistent, and record force, local extension and crosshead displacement together. Fit F=F0​+kg​ΔLg​ within that window and calculate E=kg​Lg​/A0​. Inspect the regression residuals for curvature; repeat at a lower maximum load and include unloading to check elastic deformation. These are diagnostic additions to the cited protocol, whose full test continues through failure. The handout's seating load is specific to its specimens and apparatus, rather than a universal preload.
An extensometer measures the change between its contact points; crosshead displacement measures travel of the machine's moving member. The manufacturer Instron explicitly distinguishes local strain from travel that includes machine deformation and machine compliance.[ref] The gauge length Lg​ can be shorter than the uniform length L between grips. Thus even a perfectly rigid machine generally has ΔLg​=x: the local instrument sees only its own segment. Do not divide one channel's extension by the other channel's reference length.
Grips must transmit axial force without slip. Misalignment adds bending moment and makes opposite sides experience different axial strains; an instrument on just one side may then report a biased modulus. A changing extension offset, hysteresis between loading and unloading, or load-dependent fitted slope is evidence to investigate seating, slip or material response. A straight line over a short interval alone does not identify which is responsible.

Machine compliance is the extra load-path displacement per applied force attributed to the apparatus in a specified measurement model. Its units are mN−1, the reciprocal units of a spring constant. Here Cm​ includes the frame, load cell, adapters and grips insofar as their deformation contributes to the recorded crosshead displacement x. It is a property of that configuration and readout, rather than a universal constant of the testing machine.
Assume a uniform specimen with initial length L, constant A0​ and Young's modulus E, small axial elastic deformation, quasistatic loading, no slip, and a linear, length-independent apparatus response over the chosen force window. Equilibrium makes the same force act through specimen and apparatus, while their extensions add. The two springs in series therefore give
x=x0​+EA0​FL​+Cm​F,q(L)=dFdx​=EA0​L​+Cm​,kobs​=q(L)1​.
(14)
The offset x0​ describes the displacement origin after seating; the slope q describes total compliance. Fitting an intercept avoids forcing an arbitrary zero through the origin, but cannot repair slip or a curved response.
If all of x−x0​ is incorrectly attributed to specimen extension, the inferred modulus is
Eapp​=A0​q(L)L​=1+EA0​Cm​/LE​.
(15)
For positive Cm​, this is too small. The fractional bias is most serious for a short, thick, stiff specimen because its own compliance L/(EA0​) is small. A local extensometer instead has d(ΔLg​)/dF=Lg​/(EA0​) in this ideal model, excluding deformation outside its contacts.
A shaped specimen requires more care. With varying initial cross-sectional area A(s) and uniform E, its axial compliance is ∫ds/[EA(s)] in the one-dimensional approximation. Shoulder and end deformation must be included explicitly or remain identical between tests and be absorbed into an effective intercept. Changing only the extensometer gauge length on an unchanged specimen does not change its total compliance and cannot perform a two-length machine compliance separation.

This is an inverse problem: one length supplies only one equation for two unknowns, while two distinct lengths separate the length-dependent specimen contribution from the constant contribution. In a graph of compliance against length, the slope is 1/(EA0​) and the vertical intercept is Cm​. It is the compliance, not kobs​, that is linear in L.
The dimensional analysis is revealing: [q2​−q1​]=m/N, so [(L2​−L1​)/(A0​(q2​−q1​))]=N/m2. For L2​>L1​, the ideal model requires q2​>q1​. A negative fitted Cm​ challenges the common-intercept assumptions or the measurements. Two lengths determine two parameters exactly, so they cannot test the assumed straight line; three or more lengths allow regression residuals to reveal departures. Nearly equal lengths amplify slope errors through the small difference q2​−q1​. If the actual apparatus compliances differ by ΔCm​, the inferred length slope becomes 1/(EA0​)+ΔCm​/(L2​−L1​).

Linear reversibility and yield in tensile tests
Words: 156
Tensile modulus experiment OurBigBook.com
Linearity and reversibility answer different questions. The proportional limit ends the interval in which axial stress is proportional to axial strain. Elastic deformation means that deformation is recovered after unloading; a nonlinear response can still be elastic. Conversely, a short straight portion of a loading curve does not by itself demonstrate recovery.
To check recovery, unload and examine the local extensometer strain relative to its initial value, allowing for instrument resolution, drift and any time dependence. A residual extension can indicate plasticity in continuum mechanics, but grip slip can produce a residual in crosshead displacement without the same local residual. Compare the channels before assigning the effect to the specimen. Yield point concerns the onset of irreversible deformation; a specified offset proof stress is an operational convention rather than Young's modulus. For example, a 0.2% offset proof stress is the intersection of the loading curve with σ=E(ε−0.002), using the correctly referenced strain. Report the fitted stress/strain window and the unloading evidence alongside the modulus, so that apparatus seating, departure from linearity and onset of plasticity in continuum mechanics remain distinguishable.

Eikonal equation OurBigBook.com
On an open set where u>0, put v=u​. The chain rule gives ∇u=2v∇v, so the quadratic eikonal equation is equivalent to ∣∇v∣=1. For constant positive data v=v0​ on a smooth initial curve, the tangential derivative vanishes and the two allowed normal derivatives are ∂n​v=±1. Locally the two solutions are v=v0​±d, where d is oriented distance along the normal rays; hence u=(v0​±d)2 wherever the chosen v stays positive and the normal-coordinate map remains invertible.
There are two separate obstructions to using this initial-data chart. A characteristic caustic occurs when normal rays focus and the projection Jacobian determinant vanishes. Alternatively v can reach zero while the geometric rays remain separated: the square-root transformation then ceases to apply and the original Charpit's equations have a degenerate zero-gradient state. A continuation of u beyond either obstruction needs separate justification; squaring an algebraic expression alone does not preserve a prescribed positive square-root branch.
